-<p dir="auto">This project will host the minimum guardrails as part of the GC Cloud Operationalization Framework for Oracle. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) is an approved Cloud Service Provider.</p>
-<p dir="auto">The purpose of the guardrails is to ensure that departments and agencies are implementing a preliminary baseline set of controls within their cloud-based environments.</p>
-<p dir="auto">These minimum guardrails are to be implemented within the GC-specified initial period (e.g. 30 days) upon receipt of an enrollment under the GC Cloud Services Framework Agreement.</p>
-<p dir="auto">This <a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/blob/main/docs/Guardrails%20Implementation%20Guidance%20for%20Oracle%20Cloud%20-%20EN%20(Dec%202020).pdf">document</a> provides a brief overview of each applicable guardrail and instructions on how to implement them when using OCI.</p>
-<p dir="auto">For a quicker way to deploy a secure environment fit for the Guardrails on OCI, be sure to use the OCI Landing Zone accelerator.
-See <a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/tree/main/oci-cis-landingzone-quickstart">OCI Landing Zone Quickstart</a></p>
-<p dir="auto"><a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/blob/main/docs/OCI%20Cloud%20Guardrails%20-%20EN.pdf">OCI Prowler</a> is a command-line tool that can be used to validate the guardrails implementation.</p>

-<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h1 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Mesures de sécurité du nuage pour Oracle</h1><a id="user-content-mesures-de-sécurité-du-nuage-pour-oracle" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Mesures de sécurité du nuage pour Oracle" href="#mesures-de-sécurité-du-nuage-pour-oracle"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
-<p dir="auto">Ce projet hébergera les garde-corps minimums dans le cadre de l’opérationnalisation de l’informatique en nuage du GC pour Oracle. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) est un fournisseur de services cloud approuvé.</p>
-<p dir="auto">Le but des garde-corps est de garantir que les ministères et organismes mettent en œuvre un ensemble de base de contrôle préliminaire dans leurs environnements cloud.
-Ces garde-corps minimaux doivent être mis en œuvre au cours de la période initiale spécifiée par le GC (par exemple, 30 jours) à la réception d'une inscription en vertu de l'Accord-cadre des services cloud du GC.</p>
-<p dir="auto">Ce <a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/blob/main/docs/Guardrails%20Implementation%20Guidance%20for%20Oracle%20Cloud%20-%20FR%20(Dec%202020).pdf">document</a> fournit un bref aperçu de chaque garde-corps applicable et des instructions sur la façon de les mettre en œuvre lors de l'utilisation d'OCI.</p>
-<p dir="auto">Pour un moyen plus rapide de déployer un environnement sécurisé adapté aux garde-corps sur OCI, assurez-vous d'utiliser l'accélérateur OCI Landing Zone.
-Voir <a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/tree/main/oci-cis-landingzone-quickstart">Démarrage rapide de la zone d'atterrissage OCI</a></p>
-<p dir="auto"><a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/blob/main/docs/OCI%20Cloud%20Guardrails%20-%20FR.pdf">OCI Prowler</a> est un outil de ligne de commande qui peut être utilisé pour valider l’implémentation des garde-corps.</p>

data.text:
The GitHub API is rate limited for our IP. We need to scrape the public HTML pages instead. Let's use curl to fetch the repository page and other pages. I need:

1. repo_url (already known)
2. primary_language (shown on the repo main page)
3. readme_exists (check README on main page or list files)
4. licence (check the About sidebar or license file)
5. contributing_guide (check for CONTRIBUTING.md in file list)
6. has_security_scanning_in_ci (check Actions tab HTML or workflow files)
7. has_tests_in_ci (check workflow files)
8. dependency_update_policy (check for Dependabot config files)
9. last_commit_date (latest commit on main page)
10. open_issues_count (check Issues tab)

Let's start by fetching the main repo page and issues page.

Similarly, I can look for `LICENSE` or `license` info.

For actions, the actions page might say "No workflow runs" or list workflows. Let me search for specific strings.

Let me use grep on the HTML files for specific patterns.

# Digital Standard Self-Assessment Tool

## Clone the source code to your computer

Open a command line terminal window. then clone the code to your computer

```
$ git clone https://github.com/canada-ca/digital-standards-self-assessment.git
```

## Data initialization

If you have the database in Azure cloud or in your local environment. You can initialize the data like this.

1. go to data_migration folder

```
$ cd digital-standard-self-assessment/data_migration
```

2. Install migrate-mongo globally if you don’t have it installed.

```
$ npm install -g migrate-mongo
```

3. Setup database connection in migrate-mongo-config.js
4. Initialize data. Run the following command. It will initialize the required data in database.

```
$ migrate-mongo up
```

5. Rollback data migration (if you want to roll back the date change in step 4.

```
$ migrate-mongo down
```

6. Go to your database to check if you have a database called 'dssa-db', then check if there are records the collections.

## Backend API

1. Open digital-standard-self-assessment/api folder in Visual Studio Code.
2. Press View -> Terminal to open a terminal window in VS Code.
3. Run npm install
4. Run npm start. The API local server will start up with URL [http://localhost:7071/api/](http://localhost:7071/api/)
5. Use Postman to test “Survey - Find latest”, the API will response a survey json file with HttpStatus 200.

## Frontend UI

1. Open /digital-standard-self-assessment/api folder in Visual Studio Code.
2. Press View -> Terminal to open a terminal window in VS Code.
3. Run npm install
4. Double check if the API URL is right in .env file
   VUE_APP_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:7071/api
5. Run npm run serve
6. Test the application in browser [http://localhost:8080/](http://localhost:8080/)

## Run the application in Docker container

1. Open a command line terminal, and the project folder.
2. Run "docker-compose up -d" to start all services, which includes:
   - mongodb: Mongo database
   - mongo-express: A web based GUI management tool for mongodb
   - mongo-migrate: Data migration tool to initial/update data in mongodb
   - api: Backend Azure Function APIs
   - ui: Front end application run in a Nginx server, the Nginx server also plays a reverse proxy role for the banck end API.
3. Run "docker-compose up -d \<service name\>" to start an indivial service. The \<service name\> can be:

              PROJECT_NAME: $(project)
            inputs:

              workingDirectory: "$(Build.SourcesDirectory)/infrastructure"
              addSpnToEnvironment: true
              scriptLocation: scriptPath
              scriptPath: "$(Build.SourcesDirectory)/infrastructure/helperScripts/pulumiBackendConfig.ps1"
            name: backend
            displayName: Create Backend

          - task: PublishPipelineArtifact@1
            inputs:
              targetPath: "$(Build.SourcesDirectory)/infrastructure/Pulumi.yaml"
              artifact: "pulumifile"
              publishLocation: "pipeline"
            displayName: Publish Pulumi instruction File

  - stage: "DeployDev"
    displayName: "Dev Deploy Infra & App"
    dependsOn: Pulumi
    variables:
      - group: dev
    jobs:
      - job: "Deploy_Infra"
        displayName: "Deploy Azure Resources"

        variables:
          BackendStorageKey: $[ stageDependencies.Pulumi.SetupPulumiBackend.outputs['backend.storageKey']]
          BackendContainer: $[ stageDependencies.Pulumi.SetupPulumiBackend.outputs['backend.container']]
          BackendStorageAccount: $[ stageDependencies.Pulumi.SetupPulumiBackend.outputs['backend.saAccount']]
          currentAPIM: $[ stageDependencies.Pulumi.SetupPulumiBackend.outputs['backend.currentAPIM']]

        steps:
          - template: templates/deployResources_retrieveOutputs.yaml
            parameters:
              beStorageKey: $(BackendStorageKey)
              beContainer: $(BackendContainer)
              beStorageAccount: $(BackendStorageAccount)
              azureSubscription: $(AzureSub)
              existingAPIM: $(currentAPIM)

      - job: "Deploy_API"

        dependsOn: Deploy_Infra
        condition: succeeded()
        variables:
          faName: $[ dependencies.Deploy_Infra.outputs['pulumiOutputs.faName'] ]
        steps:
          - template: templates/deploy_api.yaml
            parameters:
              faName: $(faName)
              azureSubscription: $(AzureSub)

      - job: "Configure_API_GW"
        dependsOn:
          - Deploy_Infra
          - Deploy_API

        condition: and(succeeded('Deploy_Infra'), succeeded('Deploy_API'))
        variables:
          faName: $[ dependencies.Deploy_Infra.outputs['pulumiOutputs.faName'] ]
          apiURL: $[ dependencies.Deploy_Infra.outputs['pulumiOutputs.projectAPIGW'] ]
          apiGWName: $[ dependencies.Deploy_Infra.outputs['pulumiOutputs.projectAPIGWName'] ]
          rgName: $[ dependencies.Deploy_Infra.outputs['pulumiOutputs.projectRG'] ]

        steps:
          - template: templates/configure_api_gw.yaml
            parameters:

              apiURL: $(apiURL)
              apiGWName: $(apiGWName)
              rgName: $(rgName)
              azureSubscription: $(AzureSub)

      - job: "Deploy_UI"
        dependsOn:
          - Deploy_Infra
          - Configure_API_GW
        condition: succeeded()
        variables:
          apiURL: $[ dependencies.Deploy_Infra.outputs['pulumiOutputs.projectAPIGW'] ]
          saKey: $[ dependencies.Deploy_Infra.outputs['pulumiOutputs.projectSaKey']]
          storageAccount: $[ dependencies.Deploy_Infra.outputs['pulumiOutputs.projectSA']]

        steps:
          - template: templates/deploy_ui.yaml
            parameters:
              apiURL: $(apiURL)
              saKey: $(saKey)
              storageAccount: $(storageAccount)
              azureSubscription: $(AzureSub)

      - job: "Import_Data"
